notes: FALLBACK and early start, not a replacement for Vanda: the >=256-core strong and weak cells (E3, E4) are Vanda-only, because queue parallel allows at most 96 cores per job and per user.

Serial sweep in queue serial (1 core, shared node type 'horse'); every parallel job is one whole 96-core node of pool par12, and the 1-core baselines of every speedup run inside those jobs (same node type and build as the curves).
Cores per node 96: the 33 cnode-33-* compute nodes in the discovery; pool membership of par12 was not in that discovery (the new discover.sh prints node_pool).
No GPU on Atlas: the GPU cell stays in the Vanda plan.
arithmetic: Fixed 100 iterations, 3 repeats in one process, median reported (as on Vanda).
Strong grids as on Vanda: 2D n=8192, 3D n=406 (~6.7e7 unknowns each); ranks [1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96] on one 96-core node.
Weak: ~2.1e6 unknowns per rank; at 96 ranks 2D n=14187, 3D n=586.

Serial sweep in queue serial: 2D n=[64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192], 3D n=[16, 25, 40, 64, 101, 161, 256, 406], plus iterations to tolerance; memory request 12 GB (largest classic run ~3 GB).
